description: A grouped card grid presenting each Neurathian theme as a card, badged by engagement level and divergence type, with expandable detail on Benanav's position, the divergence description, and severity rationale. Groups can be organized by engagement level (engaged vs. partial) to surface which themes received fuller uptake.

llm_extraction_schema.description: Either a flat array of card objects, or a category-keyed object whose values are arrays of card objects.

planner_hint: Use this view when the workflow has produced an engagement map for a single source thinker and the user needs to survey which themes received genuine uptake versus partial, distorted, or absent treatment. Especially useful as a first analytical view before drilling into specific anxiety-of-influence findings.

description: An accordion where each collapsible section corresponds to one SIN finding, typed by sin_type (appropriation, misreading, omission). Each panel surfaces the finding title, severity badge, target and source quotes in contrast, discrepancy analysis, and argumentative implication — allowing the critic to drill into any finding while keeping the others collapsed.

llm_extraction_schema.description: Object whose keys become accordion section headings. Each value must be an object (rendered via sub-renderer), an array (rendered as a list), or a string (rendered as prose). Numbers and booleans are rejected because they produce empty sections.

planner_hint: Recommend this view when the critic is working through Anxiety of Influence analysis and needs to inspect discrete, evidence-bearing findings — especially where sin classification, textual provenance, and argumentative consequence must be surfaced together for each finding.

description: A long-form narrative closing the page, rendering the report summary, the key divergences synthesis, sin distribution overview, and reading implications as flowing prose with optional section anchors for 'Summary,' 'Key Divergences,' 'Sin Distribution,' and 'Reading Implications.' This provides a unified interpretive conclusion after the map and findings have done their analytical work.
planner_hint: Recommend this view as the closing narrative on any anxiety-of-influence analysis page. It should appear after engagement map and individual findings views, providing the unified interpretive conclusion that ties all upstream analytical work together into a coherent portrait of the subject author's relationship to the selected source thinker.
